text:
Luke Evangelista is the new face in New Jersey, a Predators draft pick (42nd overall in 2020) who has 5 goals and 12 points in his first 19 games as a Devil. The fifth came Nov. 19 against Montreal, set up by Timo Meier and Nico Hischier, which tells you where he's playing.

The headline numbers undersell him. The Devils get about 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, almost five points better than when he sits, and both his own finishing and his linemates' are running a little below their chances. That points to more coming, not less.

This is the player Evolving-Hockey rated as worth 3.5 wins last season, 6th among all forwards, with play-driving numbers in the 95th percentile at both ends (they also noted his results ran ahead of his chances). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man: 9.1 primary shot assists per 60. His shot is soft by speed, so watch him as a passer first. The question for New Jersey is whether the production on his line catches up to how well it's been playing.
